findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources use the conventional optimal reduction to two linear robber ranges, handle the one-house boundary explicitly, and keep only two rolling prefix optima. They are concise, clear, O(n)-time and O(1)-space implementations, so no candidate is justified.

The former 256-house largest tier exceeded the source maximum of 100 houses. The benchmark now uses legal 8/64/100-house circular streets with size bound directly to n; the protected solution passes, while a correct repeated-prefix O(n^2) dynamic program passes all outputs but fails scaling (+1.11 relative exponent; 25.19x largest runtime ratio).

The already accurate derivation is retained, while the Alternatives and edge cases list now names each alternative or boundary explicitly as required. The Optimal summary now describes the exact two endpoint-excluding rolling passes instead of a generic complexity claim.
